assessmentSummary.identity: One Foot Tripod Weight Shift repetition is a bilateral standing four-direction circuit. Start centered with both heels, first metatarsal heads, fifth metatarsal heads, and relaxed toes in contact on a clean dry level surface. Shift the body mass forward until pressure increases under the forefeet without either heel lifting, return to center, shift backward without either forefoot losing contact, return to center, shift left without stepping, return to center, then shift right without stepping and return to the same centered stance. Keep every tripod contact connected, toes relaxed, knees soft and body control quiet. One complete forward, backward, left, and right circuit with all four returns is one repetition. The wall-touch version is an exact support variant. Direction-only tasks, stepping, gait, single-leg support, reaching, ankle-only rocking, short-foot doming, toe pressing, heel raising, unstable surfaces, external load, biofeedback, maximal limits testing, or clinical treatment change the variant or definition.
currentCardFindings: Source 47 has one stable legacy definition but its source variant is skeletal and does not define the four-direction sequence, center returns, contact validity, support option, pressure versus contact boundary, fatigue, duration, substitutions, or review state.

The task is not a short-foot, hallux-press, balance-hold, or heel-raise exercise. It deliberately changes pressure under a fixed bilateral base while preserving contacts and does not claim that contact means constant pressure.
Three legacy candidates returned current healthy YouTube oEmbed metadata. Two additional candidates are needed before a human can evaluate exact mechanics and accessibility; none is approved.
assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Select only when the fixed bilateral base, exact four-direction circuit, clean visible foot-safe surface, selected support, symptom and restriction screen, planned range and dose, logistics, duration, and cumulative foot, calf, balance, running, landing, jumping, agility, and lower-body budgets fit. Do not silently turn pressure shifting into a balance hold, step, gait drill, arch dome, toe press, heel raise, unstable-surface task, maximal limit test, or clinical intervention. Recompute selection, fatigue, impact, duration, logistics, substitutions, persistence, and coach and athlete rendering after every change.

calibrationEvidence.basis: Voluntary anteroposterior and mediolateral center-of-pressure research, visually guided mediolateral weight-shift research, hallux-contact limits-of-stability evidence, short-foot and hallux task mechanics, general supervised-exercise safeguards, Source 47 legacy context, and neighborhood comparison with Short-Foot Drill, Big Toe Press Iso Hold, Single-Leg Tripod Balance, and Short Foot to Calf Raise.
calibrationEvidence.uncertainty: The literature does not establish a universal excursion, circuit cadence, support position, dose, recovery interval, participant threshold, outcome, or Vortex score. Center-of-pressure studies and balance tests are not universal workout prescriptions. Human review is required for every score, relationship, and video.

currentCardSnapshot.description: Stand on a clean dry level surface with both heels, first metatarsal heads, fifth metatarsal heads, and relaxed toes in contact. Shift pressure forward, return to center, backward, return to center, left, return to center, then right and return to the same centered bilateral stance without stepping. Keep the contacts connected while pressure changes, keep toes relaxed, and use the selected hands-free or light wall-touch support. One full four-direction circuit is one repetition.

evidence.sourceTitle: Evaluation of the postural stability in man: movement and posture interaction
claims: The study measured deliberate anteroposterior and mediolateral pressure excursions during standing tasks.
Vortex defines a fixed-base four-direction shift with an explicit center return after each excursion; it does not label it an arch dome or balance hold.

evidence.sourceTitle: Effects of Filtering the Center of Pressure Feedback Provided in Visually Guided Mediolateral Weight Shifting
claims: Mediolateral weight shifting is a distinct center-of-pressure task.
Directional pressure shifts, stepping, gait, and unilateral balance remain separate movement contracts.

evidence.sourceTitle: The influence of body posture and added mass on intrinsic and extrinsic foot muscle activation and force output during common foot strengthening exercises
evidence.sourcePublisher: Journal of Foot and Ankle Research
claims: Standing foot tasks involve intrinsic and extrinsic foot contributors within whole-body postural control.
The card records foot, ankle, calf, knee, hip, and trunk roles without claiming isolated muscle action.

evidence.sourceTitle: Effects of Filtering the Center of Pressure Feedback Provided in Visually Guided Mediolateral Weight Shifting
claims: Center-of-pressure motion can precede and guide a mediolateral body-weight transfer.
Contact retention is not a claim of constant pressure; the task uses controlled pressure redistribution within a fixed bilateral base.

evidence.sourceTitle: Evaluation of the postural stability in man: movement and posture interaction
claims: Voluntary sway requires precise control of body position in both sagittal and frontal directions.
Candidate scores describe task complexity and physical demand only; they do not classify people.

evidence.sourceTitle: The influence of body posture and added mass on intrinsic and extrinsic foot muscle activation and force output during common foot strengthening exercises
evidence.sourcePublisher: Journal of Foot and Ankle Research
claims: Body posture changes activation and force behavior during weightbearing foot tasks.
Acute laboratory observations do not establish workout fatigue or recovery, so Vortex tracks valid circuits, range, support, faults, symptoms, and overlapping lower-body exposure.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Resistance Training: Updated Position Statement Paper From the NSCA
claims: General training safeguards require safe environments, progressive exposure, instruction, and supervision appropriate to the task.
Vortex requires a clean dry level surface, toe and foot visibility, adequate space, selected support, communication, and exit conditions without demographic classification.

evidence.sourceTitle: Evaluation of the postural stability in man: movement and posture interaction
claims: The research uses controlled task trials rather than a universal workout protocol.
Candidate circuit ranges are planning proposals and stop before contact, balance, breathing, or symptom quality degrades.

evidence.sourceTitle: Effects of Filtering the Center of Pressure Feedback Provided in Visually Guided Mediolateral Weight Shifting
claims: Visualized targets can direct a mediolateral center-of-pressure shift.
Vortex uses observable direction, center return, no-step, retained-contact, and calm-body cues without requiring instrumented feedback.

evidence.sourceTitle: Noncontact of the unilateral hallux with the ground reduces forward limits of stability while standing
claims: Hallux contact affected forward limits of stability in the study conditions.
Stop if contacts, balance, control, symptoms, or the safe station cannot be restored; do not force an end-range shift.

evidence.sourceTitle: Effect of intrinsic foot muscles training on foot function and dynamic postural balance: A systematic review and meta-analysis
claims: Intrinsic-foot intervention studies are heterogeneous in exercise selection and outcome measures.
The task can serve preparation or low-fatigue control only when purpose and downstream balance and lower-body budgets fit; no universal transfer is promised.

evidence.sourceTitle: Effects of Filtering the Center of Pressure Feedback Provided in Visually Guided Mediolateral Weight Shifting
claims: A left-right target can make the shift direction observable.
Athlete support uses one direction at a time, a small smooth shift, a center reset, relaxed toes, and a stop-before-loss rule.

evidence.sourceTitle: Evaluation of the postural stability in man: movement and posture interaction
claims: Anteroposterior and mediolateral excursions can be observed as distinct tasks.
Coaches record direction, center return, contacts, stepping, toe gripping, body strategy, support, first fault, symptoms, and actual dose without diagnosing impairment.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Resistance Training: Updated Position Statement Paper From the NSCA
claims: Instruction, environment, progression, and supervision should be matched to the actual task and setting.
Smaller excursion, wall-touch, fewer circuits, longer rest, clear directional markers, captions, stills, transcript, and live verbal instruction can improve access while preserving the contract.

evidence.sourceTitle: The influence of body posture and added mass on intrinsic and extrinsic foot muscle activation and force output during common foot strengthening exercises
evidence.sourcePublisher: Journal of Foot and Ankle Research
claims: Short-foot, hallux-flexion, and heel-raise tasks are separately described in the study protocol.
Pressure shifts, arch shortening, hallux pressing, and heel raises have explicit boundaries; support and direction changes are assessed rather than silently collapsed.
YouTube supports embedded playback subject to video and platform state.
Three legacy candidates returned healthy oEmbed metadata on 2026-08-09; additional candidates and complete mechanics, accessibility, quality, and approval review remain pending.

alternateAssessments.name: Bilateral Hands-Free Four-Direction Foot Tripod Weight Shift
alternateAssessments.rationale: Authored exact source circuit with a fixed bilateral base and all four center returns.

alternateAssessments.name: Wall-Touch Four-Direction Foot Tripod Weight Shift
alternateAssessments.rationale: Light wall contact changes support while preserving the same fixed-base circuit.

alternateAssessments.name: Smaller Comfortable Weight Shift
alternateAssessments.rationale: Excursion amplitude is dosage while direction, contacts, base, and sequence remain intact.

alternateAssessments.name: Slower or Faster Clean Circuit Tempo
alternateAssessments.rationale: Tempo changes exposure but not the four-direction return contract.

alternateAssessments.name: Directional Cue Marker Change
alternateAssessments.rationale: A visual or verbal direction cue does not change the physical task.

alternateAssessments.name: Circuit Repetition Set or Rest Change
alternateAssessments.rationale: Volume and recovery are delivery fields.

alternateAssessments.name: Comfortable Stance Width
alternateAssessments.rationale: A small stance-width adjustment is an annotation when no stepping or support change occurs.

alternateAssessments.name: Footwear Within Approved Traction and Visibility Rules
alternateAssessments.rationale: Foot covering is operational when contact observation and traction remain adequate.

alternateAssessments.name: Breathing Prompt
alternateAssessments.rationale: Breathing cues do not change identity unless breath control becomes the task.

alternateAssessments.name: Forward-Backward Foot Tripod Weight Shift Only
alternateAssessments.rationale: Removing mediolateral excursions changes sequence, dose, and observation.

alternateAssessments.name: Left-Right Foot Tripod Weight Shift Only
alternateAssessments.rationale: Removing sagittal excursions changes sequence, dose, and observation.

alternateAssessments.name: Circular Foot Tripod Weight Shift
alternateAssessments.rationale: A circular trajectory changes sequence and center-return criteria.

alternateAssessments.name: Single-Leg Tripod Weight Shift
alternateAssessments.rationale: Unilateral support changes load, balance, fall response, and count.

alternateAssessments.name: Split-Stance Weight Shift
alternateAssessments.rationale: Split stance changes base geometry and directional interpretation.

alternateAssessments.name: Stepping Weight Shift
alternateAssessments.rationale: A step changes base, locomotion, contacts, and count.

alternateAssessments.name: Unstable-Surface Weight Shift
alternateAssessments.rationale: Surface compliance changes balance, logistics, and failure behavior.

alternateAssessments.name: Externally Loaded Weight Shift
alternateAssessments.rationale: External resistance changes force path, handling, and fatigue.

alternateAssessments.name: Short-Foot Drill
alternateAssessments.rationale: Arch shortening and an isometric hold are a different primary action.

alternateAssessments.name: Big Toe Press Iso Hold
alternateAssessments.rationale: A sustained hallux press is not a whole-foot pressure circuit.

alternateAssessments.name: Toe Yoga
alternateAssessments.rationale: Selective toe extension is not whole-foot pressure transfer.

alternateAssessments.name: Single-Leg Tripod Balance
alternateAssessments.rationale: A static unilateral hold has a different base, action, and count.

alternateAssessments.name: Short Foot to Calf Raise
alternateAssessments.rationale: An arch action followed by bilateral plantarflexion is a compound sequence.

alternateAssessments.name: Knee-to-Wall Ankle Rocker
alternateAssessments.rationale: Knee-forward dorsiflexion uses a different action and endpoint.

alternateAssessments.name: Limits-of-Stability Assessment
alternateAssessments.rationale: Maximal excursion testing changes intent, measurement, risk, and stop rules.
